newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends higher on foreign fund inflows.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends higher on foreign fund inflows.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed higher against the U.S. dollar on Tuesday amid foreign fund inflows and tightening liquidity in the local money market, dealers said.
The local unit ended at T$27.521 against Monday's T$27.530 close, off an intraday high of T$27.505.
Turnover through dealers was an active US$292 million.
Dealers said they saw foreign fund inflows in morning trade, pushing up the local dollar to its intraday high, but that countervailing demand for greenbacks emerged later.
"Strong U.S. dollar demand emerged in afternoon trade to offset the Taiwan dollar appreciation," said one dealer.
The central bank had issued negotiable certificates of deposit in recent sessions to mop up excess money in a bid to cool down the red-hot stock market, dealers said.
The tightening liquidity has expanded the interest rate differentials between the Taiwan dollar and the U.S. dollar, triggering some U.S. dollar selling, dealers said.
The local dollar's overnight interbank rate was around 6.5 percent while the greenback's was only 5.25 percent, they said.
For Wednesday, a T$27.50-27.54 range was seen.
